non_blocking_notes: Moira's assignment model is reporter/presenter attribution on each story (reporterId/presenterId), not a separate task object, task list, or task due-time field. The batch and research correctly avoid claiming a task module, but the leaf's assignment-and-task branch is only minimally realized; schedule-derived clock/backtime is the only deadline mechanism.

There is no distinct unscheduled backlog or pitch area: addStory() inserts a new story directly into the running order before the end marker, so the leaf rule that scheduled and unscheduled are distinct states is not demonstrated.

Producer/Reporter/Presenter are staff labels, and rundown locking is a collaborative editor lock rather than enforced authorization; Firestore rules in instructions/firestore.md allow any authenticated session to read/write bulletins and rundown_stories. Producer-managed is a workflow description, not a permission check, and the product should not be described as role-based access control.

The trash/restore feature is session-local (state.ui.trash, labelled 'deleted ... this session'), not a persistent trash collection; the batch does not claim permanence, but downstream copy should not imply it.

Moira is a single-file browser app with optional Firebase/Firestore sync, not a multi-tenant SaaS; the case is explicitly scoped to the broadcast-bulletin realization. The leaf definition names no deployment form, so this is a scope caveat rather than a type mismatch.
The README snapshot is only 28 lines and ends mid-changelog; core workflow claims were verified against moira.html and instructions/firestore.md, not README or repository metadata alone.

research.json cites historical Superdesk fetch outcomes (llms.txt SHA, Broadcasting 404, docs repository tree) whose snapshots are not in this unit's REVIEW_SOURCES.json; they are not needed for the Moira match, but those negative claims cannot be independently re-verified from this unit.

batch.json's leaf_matches.source_urls omits the license API and raw LICENSE URLs even though the reason cites the MIT license; the entry-level sources and license_evidence_url include both, so there is no evidence gap.
The repository is wholly MIT with no separate commercial/community edition, so no open-core boundary exists; the complete LICENSE and GitHub license API both confirm MIT.

newsroom-management-system.definition_core: Verified against moira.html: persistent story records in Firestore (slug, format, reporterId, presenterId, duration, script, mediaFile), running order with drag/up-down reordering, per-story TX clock from txClockTime plus accumulated durations, backtime from scheduled end versus projected end, floated-story exclusion, TX On Air/Preview Next, presenter/autocue, roles, rundown lock, and trash/restore. This supports the work-item and timed ordered broadcast-rundown pillars.
newsroom-management-system.assignment_task_scope: People are bound to stories through reporterId/presenterId only; no separate task entity, task list, or task due-time field was found. The second pillar is minimal; urgency comes from the rundown clock/backtime. This limitation is disclosed in research.json and is treated as a scope note.
newsroom-management-system.service_form: Browser-delivered single-page app with optional Firebase/Firestore real-time sync and a hosted demo; continuously usable as a newsroom system, but self-hosted/single-tenant rather than multi-tenant SaaS.
newsroom-management-system.id_track: Repository metadata snapshot gives id 1178344846 and full_name digitaldickinson/moira, matching batch github:1178344846; public repository with MIT license, so track open_source is correct.
newsroom-management-system.license: Complete MIT LICENSE (Copyright (c) 2026 Andy Dickinson) and GitHub license API both confirm MIT; no missing license file. The entire repository is MIT, so no community-edition boundary or open-core split applies.
newsroom-management-system.boundary: Moira ends at rundown/playout (radio/OBS) and has no publication, correction, retraction, legal-archive, or front-page curation workflow, so it does not conflict with the leaf rule that the system ends at the public record.
newsroom-management-system.source_basis: Read all seven REVIEW_SOURCES snapshots: repository metadata, license API, raw LICENSE, README, CHANGELOG, instructions/firestore.md, and moira.html. Batch claims about story fields, reordering, clocks/backtime, roles, lock, float, trash, and playout are supported by the application source; README and firestore.md support product identity and multi-user sync.
